tailMarker.anomalyNote: No §3.1 anomaly by the letter: rank 6 > 3 and conditioning ingredients (Cetearyl Alcohol @2, Cetrimonium Chloride @4, Quaternium-18 @5) precede the marker. But the marker is unusually early relative to list length (6 of 34), so the entire marketed payload — Argania Spinosa Kernel Oil @7, five protein species @8/@10/@11/@13/@14, Glycerin @19, Panthenol @20, Sodium PCA @22 — falls in the tail and earns nothing. This is the cohort's most extreme hero-tail structure.

conditioningLevel.evidenceScope: Formula-only, exact-market DE INCI of record (sha256 dff721bd…), above-tail ranks 1–5; category-relative to the German drugstore rinse-out mask shelf.
conditioningLevel.rationale: Two of the three §9.1 structural signals are satisfied inside a five-entry above-tail segment that contains nothing but conditioning architecture. E2 ceiling: this is comparative structural intensity potential, not measured treatment performance.
evidenceSignals: CETRIMONIUM CHLORIDE (rank 4) — long-chain cationic quat, above tail
QUATERNIUM-18 (rank 5) — second, structurally distinct dialkyl cationic quat, above tail
CETEARYL ALCOHOL (rank 2) — long-chain fatty alcohol in the top three of the full list
LANOLIN (rank 3) — sole non-fatty-alcohol lipid above the tail
conditioningLevel.derivation: S1 (cationic breadth, ≥2 distinct species above tail) = satisfied by Cetrimonium Chloride @4 + Quaternium-18 @5. S2 (fatty alcohol at rank 2 or 3 of the full list) = satisfied by Cetearyl Alcohol @2. S3 (≥2 distinct non-fatty-alcohol lipids above tail) = NOT satisfied — Lanolin @3 is the only one; Argania Spinosa Kernel Oil @7 and Isopropyl Palmitate @21 are in the tail. Count = 2 of 3.
thresholdReasoning: Clears `high`: §9.1 sets `high` at ≥2 of {S1,S2,S3} with no material counter-signal. Two signals are satisfied and neither of §9.1's named counter-signals (rheology-only ingredients, long ingredient list, sub-1% hero tail) moves a value in any direction.
`moderate` does not apply: §9.1 assigns `moderate` to 'everything else, including exactly one satisfied signal'. Two signals are satisfied, so the moderate bucket is not reached.
`low` does not apply: `low` requires none of S1/S2/S3, i.e. a single cationic species, no fatty alcohol in the top three, and at most one lipid above the tail. The first two conditions fail outright.
counterSignals: S1 depends on QUATERNIUM-18 at rank 5, i.e. tail_index − 1. Under the lexicon §0.2 boundary-band caution this dependency caps confidence (it does not move the value).
The above-tail segment is only five entries long; a single transcription slip in a fallback-tier source would change the signal count.
Argania Spinosa Kernel Oil @7 and five protein species in the tail are a textbook sub-1% hero tail (§9.1 named counter-signal) — recorded, not credited.
limitations: A three-step concentration scale is at the edge of INCI support; no published dataset maps INCI patterns to validated low/medium/high thresholds (§9.1 honest limitation).
Source is hautschutzengel fallback tier; dm.de is JS-rendered and could not be fetched.
Rank is used qualitatively only. EU Art. 19 hides the 1% boundary; no percentage, ratio, or dose is inferable.

weightPotential.evidenceScope: Formula-only, above-tail ranks 1–5; an ingredient-informed matching prior, not a prediction of visible flattening.
weightPotential.rationale: The §9.2 rich-base condition is met and is joined by a heavy occlusive lipid at rank 3 — the highest-ranked heavy lipid in the whole cohort. E2 ceiling: weight deposition potential, never measured finish.
evidenceSignals: CETRIMONIUM CHLORIDE (rank 4) + QUATERNIUM-18 (rank 5) — two distinct cationics above the tail
CETEARYL ALCOHOL (rank 2) — cetearyl-class fatty alcohol in the top three
LANOLIN (rank 3) — heavy occlusive wax-ester lipid above the tail
weightPotential.derivation: §9.2 required base = ≥2 distinct cationics above the tail AND a cetearyl-class fatty alcohol in the top three: both met. Supporting alternative (a) = an R4b heavy lipid above the tail: Lanolin @3 is read as R4b (heavy occlusive lipid, functionally alongside the lexicon family-3 heavy band Cera Alba/Petrolatum). Alternative (b) occlusive silicone stack: not present (no silicone above the tail; the siloxysilicate protein @8 is in the tail).
thresholdReasoning: Clears `high`: the base-plus-one-alternative structure ruled by Nick 2026-09-04 (§9.2 [RULED]) is satisfied — base met, alternative (a) met, and there is no material unresolved counter-signal from exact-product positioning.
`moderate` does not apply: `moderate` is 'everything else' once the high anchor fails. The anchor does not fail here unless Lanolin is denied R4b status — the single hinge, recorded below.
`low` does not apply: `low` requires a single cationic species AND no cetearyl-class fatty alcohol in the top three AND no R4b heavy lipid above the tail. All three conditions fail.
§9.2 conflict fallback not triggered: no lightness positioning. The claims are 'nährt und revitalisiert trockenes, strapaziertes Haar' — consistent with, not contradicting, a rich prior.
counterSignals: LANOLIN is named in neither the standard's R4b enumeration nor the lexicon family-3 heavy band. Its R4b classification is a reviewer judgment and is the sole hinge of the `high` value (AP-01-LANOLIN).
Silicone status is irrelevant here (§9.2: silicone presence is not the weight driver) — recorded so it is not mistaken for support.
limitations: Weight drives a soft preference with a stated reason, never an exclusion; fine-hair flattening is a fit mismatch, not a hair-type law (§9.2 wording rule).
Lanolin's occlusivity is a well-known formulation property but the deposited amount from a rinse-out mask is not inferable from an INCI list.

careDirection.evidenceScope: Formula-only, above-tail ranks 1–5; comparative care emphasis, never an assertion about a user's protein or moisture state (G6).
careDirection.rationale: The above-tail architecture is a pure cationic/fatty-alcohol/lipid conditioning base with no protein or peptide species in it at all; every protein token in this product sits in the tail and is therefore non-contributing. Under D6 that is the coherent non-protein direction. E2 ceiling: comparative emphasis, not a delivered outcome.
evidenceSignals: CETEARYL ALCOHOL (2), LANOLIN (3), CETRIMONIUM CHLORIDE (4), QUATERNIUM-18 (5) — the complete above-tail care architecture

HYDROXYPROPYLTRIMONIUM HYDROLYZED ORYZA SATIVA PROTEIN/SILOXYSILICATE (8), HYDROLYZED COLLAGEN (10), HYDROLYZED KERATIN (11), HYDROLYZED SOY PROTEIN (13), SODIUM LAUROYL OAT AMINO ACIDS (14) — all in the tail, zero credit
SILK AMINO ACIDS (12) — free-amino-acid class, an explicit R5 non-qualifier even if it were above the tail
GLYCERIN (19), PANTHENOL (20), SODIUM PCA (22), BUTYLENE GLYCOL (25) — humectants, all in the tail
careDirection.derivation: §9.3 material-R5 test: a qualifying R5 species above the tail is required before either leg (a) or (b) can be considered. There is none, so `protein` is unreachable. §9.3 `balanced` test requires the material R5 route as its first conjunct, so `balanced` is unreachable too. The residual value is `moisture`, which D6 defines as the category's honest default: a coherent conditioning/humectant/emollient architecture without a dominant protein-film route.
thresholdReasoning: Clears `moisture`: the above-tail set is a coherent conditioning/emollient architecture (fatty alcohol + heavy lipid + two cationics) and carries no protein-film route.

`protein` does not apply: it requires a material identifiable R5 route. Zero qualifying R5 species appear above the tail; Silk Amino Acids is additionally excluded as a free amino acid (R5 mask delta).

`balanced` does not apply: D6 reserves it for a substantive mixed protein-plus-moisture architecture and forbids it as a 'neither' bucket. The protein leg is absent, so the reserved value is not available.
counterSignals: The exact-product positioning is protein- and oil-led ('reich an Antioxidantien, Fettsäuren', 'verbessert sichtbar die Haarstruktur') and the list carries five protein species — a strong claim/formula divergence. Recorded per §9.3 ('Protein naming with the protein only in the tail → moisture, with the claim recorded'); it never moves the value.

The whole call rests on tail_index = 6. A reviewer who instead took the preservative block (DMDM Hydantoin @24) as the marker would place five proteins above the tail and reach `protein` or `balanced` — a two-step swing. This is the single largest tail-rule sensitivity in the cohort (AP-01-TAILSWING).
limitations: INCI discloses no molecular weight, so even a credited hydrolysed protein could only support 'a protein film route is present'.
D4 protein-payload counter-signal did NOT fire here despite five protein species, because its detection threshold is above-tail-gated (AP-D4-BLINDSPOT).

evidenceSignals: no maleate, gluconamide, or bond-positioned peptide token at any rank
HYDROLYZED COLLAGEN (10), HYDROLYZED KERATIN (11), HYDROLYZED SOY PROTEIN (13) — in the tail
LANOLIN (3), CETRIMONIUM CHLORIDE (4), QUATERNIUM-18 (5) — ordinary R1/R4 conditioning, explicit non-upgraders

`medium` does not apply: it needs a distinct temporary protein/peptide/keratin fibre-film route above the tail; every protein species is in the tail and a tail-position protein is an explicit non-upgrader.
`high` does not apply: nothing but a named bond token above the tail reaches `high`, and none exists.
Mask delta applied: conditioning_level `high` alone is repair_support_level `low`; being a rich mask is not repair.

primaryFocus.evidenceScope: Formula-first §9.5.2 hierarchy over above-tail ranks 1–5; claims used only where §11 step 4 permits.
primaryFocus.rationale: Every special-purpose route fails on its own test, the moisture guard fails on cluster size, the shine threshold fails for want of any optical-emphasis architecture above the tail, and the smoothing threshold fails its 'dry surface control is the clearest practical differentiator' conjunct. §9.5.2 step 8 is the honest fallback: a capable conventional rich mask with no differentiator clearing threshold.
evidenceSignals: LANOLIN (3) — substantial emollient route beyond baseline, but a softening/occlusive route rather than a dry-surface-control route
no silicone, cationic polymer, or film former above the tail (the siloxysilicate protein sits at rank 8, in the tail)
zero humectants above the tail
claims: 'entwirrt und zähmt widerspenstiges Haar' — detangling/taming positioning, corroboration only
primaryFocus.derivation: Step 1 baseline exclusion applied (rich R1+R4 base does not create a focus). Step 2 mechanism grouping: the entire above-tail set is one M1 observation. Step 3: `repair` blocked (no R5 above tail, no bond); `curl_support` blocked (no curl positioning and slip is baseline); `color_care` blocked (no candidate, no positioning); `lightness` blocked (weight_potential is `high`, not `low`). Step 4 `moisture` blocked (zero humectants above the tail). Step 5 `shine` blocked (§9.5.4 criterion 1 fails outright). Step 6 `smoothing` rejected (see below). Step 7 `detangling` rejected. Step 8 → `general`.
thresholdReasoning: Clears `general`: §9.5.2 step 8 — a capable conventional mask where no specific focus clears the differentiator threshold and the formula evidence is nonspecific.

`smoothing` (the closest competitor) does not apply: step 6 is a conjunction. The second conjunct is arguably met — Lanolin @3 is a substantial emollient route beyond baseline — but the first is not: dry surface control is not this formula's clearest practical differentiator, because the only route beyond the base is a softening occlusive, with no silicone, no substantive polymer, and no film former above the tail.

`detangling` does not apply: §9.5.2 step 7 permits it only when slip is itself distinctive. Two cationics above the tail is the category's own baseline-to-slightly-above band, and the 'entwirrt' claim can corroborate but never create (step 9).
`moisture` does not apply: the D5 guard needs ≥3 distinct humectants above the tail with ≥2 non-glycerin. The count above the tail is zero.
counterSignals: The product's marketing identity (Argan Oil, five proteins) points at repair/nourishment; none of it is above the tail, so none of it may create a route (§9.5.2 step 9).
limitations: `general` here is a statement about what the evidence supports, not a judgment that the product is weak.

secondaryFocus.rationale: With `general` as the forced headline — meaning no candidate cleared its differentiator threshold — no secondary can add distinct matching information without re-importing a route that was just rejected.
evidenceSignals: no route above the tail beyond the single M1 observation
secondaryFocus.derivation: A secondary must represent a distinct user endpoint AND add useful matching information (§9.5.2 secondary rule). Every candidate here would reuse the same M1 lanolin/cationic film that failed to clear as primary.
thresholdReasoning: Zero secondaries is the correct count: the vocabulary permits 0–2, and awarding `smoothing` or `detangling` as a secondary after rejecting both as primary would be double-counting the one M1 mechanism (§6 rule 1).

focusCareVerdict.note: Generic intensive conditioning above the tail is compatible with both a repair and a moisture reading and distinguishes neither. Per §9.5.1 a `nonspecific` verdict resolves to `general` unless the dry-surface route genuinely clears §9.5.2 step 6; it does not here. No claim was used: the product's repair/oil positioning could not convert nonspecific formula evidence into a specialist focus.

blindToFinalChanges.reason: Unblinding produced no change. Claims were checked only against the four channels §11 step 4 permits: no shine corroboration was sought (the shine threshold failed at criterion 1 before claims were consulted), no dual_supported tie existed, no bond claim was made, no lightness positioning existed to trigger the §9.2 conflict fallback, and no colour-protection positioning existed.

adjudicationPoints.title: LANOLIN is unclassified by both the standard's R4a/R4b split and the lexicon's lipid bands
adjudicationPoints.body: Lanolin sits at rank 3 — the highest-ranked non-fatty-alcohol lipid position in the entire cohort — but appears in neither §5 R4b's enumeration (butters, heavy triglycerides, hydrogenated oils, occlusive hydrocarbons) nor lexicon family 3's heavy band (which names Cera Alba and Petrolatum, its closest functional relatives). I classified it R4b on functional grounds. That single reading is the sole hinge of weight_potential `high`; rejecting it drops the field to `moderate` and widens hair_thickness_fit to include `fine`. The lexicon needs an explicit lanolin/wool-wax entry.

adjudicationPoints.title: Tail rule alone separates a five-protein 'repair' mask from a plain conditioning base
adjudicationPoints.body: With tail_index = 6 (Parfum), this product's five protein species, its hero argan oil, and all four humectants are non-contributing, giving care_direction `moisture` and repair_support_level `low`. Under any alternative marker choice that reached the preservative block (DMDM Hydantoin @24), the same list would produce a material R5 route with three-plus species, care_direction `protein` or `balanced`, repair_support_level `medium`, and a specialist damage_fit of moderately+highly damaged. The rule is doing more work on this product than on any other in the cohort, and the outcome is entirely reproducible — but only because §3.1's marker choice is mechanical, not because the underlying formulation fact is settled.

adjudicationPoints.title: The D4 protein-payload counter-signal cannot fire on the cohort's largest protein payload
adjudicationPoints.body: §13's detection threshold is 'multiple distinct R5 species above the tail, and/or a qualifying R5 species in the top five ranks'. This product declares five protein species plus a free-amino-acid token — the heaviest protein payload in the cohort — and D4 does not fire, because every one of them is in the tail. The rule is coherent (tail ingredients earn nothing) but its stated purpose, flagging heavy protein payloads for human review, is defeated exactly where a human would most want the flag.

adjudicationPoints.title: §2.1's 'to lengths and ends' conjunct is unmet verbatim on most of the cohort
adjudicationPoints.body: §2.1 defines eligibility as a rinse-out treatment applied after cleansing TO LENGTHS AND ENDS with a stated contact time, then rinsed. Only 4 of 12 eligible cohort products state placement in their authoritative directions (#03, #06, #08, #10). Enforcing the conjunct literally would exclude two thirds of the shelf and collide with the charter's ≥80% coverage target and its own named inclusions. I did not refuse eligibility on placement anywhere; placement is TPL-MASK/P5's slot, not a G0 boundary test. The standard should either drop the conjunct from G0 or state that unstated placement defaults to the P5 canonical placement.

assumptionNotes: Reviewer policy applied to every record in this lane: §3.1's hard cut (strictly before tail_index) determines above-tail membership without exception; the lexicon §0.2 boundary-band caution is applied only as a confidence modifier where a threshold's satisfaction depends on an ingredient at tail_index − 1, and never moves a value.
